titleStmt.title: Hypergraph Reduction via Hypertree Decomposition and Case-Based Reasoning

analytic.title: Hypergraph Reduction via Hypertree Decomposition and Case-Based Reasoning

abstract.p: In this paper, we propose Hypertree Decomposition-Based Hypergraph Reduction (HD-HR) augmented by Case-Based Reasoning (CBR). Large hypergraph structures in combinatorial optimization represent NP-complete computational complexity problems. By leveraging Graph Theory and structural tree width bounds, our approach extracts tree projections to solve intractable constraint satisfaction problems efficiently.

div.head: 1. Introduction and Complexity Background
div.p: Constraint satisfaction and combinatorial optimization problems often exhibit intractable Computational Complexity, categorized as NP-complete [1]. Graph Theory provides formal foundations for analyzing relational structures.

div.head: 2. Structural Graph Foundations
div.p: A hypergraph is formalized as a vertex and hyperedge system:

Standard Graph Traversal algorithms such as depth-first search (DFS) fail on cyclic hypergraphs. Instead, Hypertree Decomposition partitions vertices into acyclic generalized tree nodes with bounded hypertree width.

div.head: 3. Case-Based Reasoning Integration
div.p: Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) retrieves past successful decomposition topologies from an indexed knowledge base [2]. Rather than computing decompositions from scratch, CBR guides subproblem solving.

div.head: 4. Proposed Methodology: Hypertree Decomposition-Based Hypergraph Reduction
div.p: We propose Hypertree Decomposition-Based Hypergraph Reduction. Hypergraph Reduction prunes redundant hyperedges while preserving satisfiability. The hypertree decomposition structure guarantees polynomial-time evaluation.
